I hypothesize that Reddit's content heavily influences the top content on Voat, making the 2 sites for all intents and purposes one and the same. If we are to maintain our independence and cultural superiority I suggest we investigate this phenomenon in depth and root out it's causal agents.

I can't find this same post on Reddit, so there's that.
Both are content aggregates so it makes sense the content will be similar. where they differ is the discussion of that content.

If most people like X and X is posted to Reddit, it will be upvoted.

If most people like X and X is posted to Voat, it will be upvoated.

If most people want to talk about X but mods don't like X you won't find it on Reddit.

If most people want to talk about X but mods don't like X you can still find it on Voat.

Wait, you're telling me that popular memes and information spread across multiple websites? NO WAY.

That's how the internet works. Trying to isolate Voat (a Reddit clone) from Reddit is a stupid idea.
